posts.title: Accurate and well-powered case-control analysis of spatial molecular data
posts.authors: Reshef YA, Sood L, Curtis M, et al.
posts.summary: VIMA (variational inference-based microniche analysis) finds disease-associated spatial features without forcing tissue into discrete cell types or niches. An ensemble of variational autoencoders gives every small tissue patch a numeric fingerprint, and these define many overlapping, data-dependent microniches whose abundance is tested against case-control status.
key_points: Simulations confirm VIMA's calibration, power and spatial accuracy.
It was applied to spatial datasets spanning three diseases and spatial modalities, recapitulating known biology.
It also identified new spatial features of disease.

figure.caption: Patch fingerprints from a VAE ensemble define overlapping microniches, and those whose abundance differs between case and control tissue are flagged.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Chromatin accessibility trajectories reveal pre-cancerous epigenetic priming and an acid-driven immunotherapy-resistant gastric cancer subtype
posts.authors: Wang T, Xiang J, Tian S, et al.
posts.summary: A chromatin accessibility atlas of 650 multistage samples from 439 patients maps the epigenetic switches across stepwise gastric tumorigenesis. Advanced tumours split into three epigenomic subtypes, one of which is intrinsically resistant to neoadjuvant immunotherapy.
key_points: A cancer-resembling epigenetic priming state already exists in intestinal metaplasia and licenses later tumour initiation.
The proliferative and mesenchymal-inflammatory subtypes respond to neoadjuvant immunotherapy, while the pseudo-gastric subtype is drug resistant.

In the resistant subtype, FOSL2 helps raise H/K ATPase transporters and builds an acidic milieu that suppresses CD8 T cells; FOSL2 depletion or the acid blocker vonoprazan sensitizes to immunotherapy.

figure.caption: Chromatin states step from normal stomach through intestinal metaplasia to cancer, and in the resistant subtype FOSL2 drives acid that suppresses CD8 T cells.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Benchmarking copy number alteration inference methods for spatial transcriptomics
posts.authors: Han S, Xiong Z, Zhou Y, et al.
posts.summary: Direct spatial genomic profiling is hard, so copy number alterations are often inferred from spatial transcriptomics. This benchmark compares nine such inference methods across 69 tissue sections from six cancer types and four platforms.
key_points: Methods were evaluated on four key tasks.
No single method consistently outperforms the others; performance depends on the analytical goal and the data.
The authors give task-specific, data-aware guidance for choosing a method.

posts.title: Cost-efficient long-read trio-barcoded adaptive sequencing improves rare disease diagnosis
posts.authors: Fu Y, English AC, Paulin LF, et al.
posts.summary: TBAS barcodes an affected child and both parents and runs them on one Oxford Nanopore flow cell, using adaptive sequencing to enrich phenotype-driven disease-gene panels. It makes long-read trio analysis cheaper without needing to know the causal locus.
key_points: In benchmark regions it raised coverage and accurately detected small variants, structural variants, tandem repeat expansions, methylation and phasing.
Estimated consumable cost fell to 32.2% of conventional three-flow-cell trio long-read sequencing.
Across 13 trios it recovered all five known diagnoses and prioritized candidates in five of eight unresolved cases.

posts.title: Rapid Whole Genome Sequencing Enhances Pediatric Cancer Diagnosis
posts.authors: Vedi A, Trotman J, Dias JML, et al.
posts.summary: A rapid whole-genome sequencing (rWGS) research workflow with streamlined bioinformatics was tested in 54 children with suspected or confirmed cancer. It aims to return clinically actionable genomic findings in days rather than weeks.
key_points: Mean end-to-end turnaround dropped from 42 to 3 days.
rWGS detected 147 of 155 (95%) clinically actionable variants, versus 138 of 155 (89%) for standard-of-care testing.
In 35 prospectively assessed patients, clinicians said rWGS sped targeted therapy and risk stratification or avoided unnecessary treatment escalation in 17 (49%).

posts.title: STiLE: Automated Tissue Microarray Dearraying for Spatial Transcriptomics
posts.authors: Sinha H, Das A, Chiu YC, et al.
posts.summary: STiLE assigns cells to their tissue microarray cores using only cell centroid coordinates, removing the manual dearraying bottleneck and any dependence on histology images. It combines connectivity-based component detection, HDBSCAN clustering, cluster merging and optional grid-based peak detection.
key_points: On seven public TMA samples (50-150 cores, three platforms) it reached ARI > 0.99.
On 396 synthetic datasets with realistic artefacts, mean ARI was 0.992.
It is platform-agnostic (MERSCOPE, Xenium, CosMx), reads AnnData and CSV, and has an interactive Streamlit interface.

posts.title: ProxiNet transfers spatially learned cellular proximity to dissociated single-cell transcriptomes
posts.authors: Zhan Y, Yan B, Zhang A, et al.
posts.summary: ProxiNet learns transcriptomic signatures of pairwise cellular proximity from spatial reference data and transfers them to dissociated scRNA-seq, which has lost neighbourhood information.
key_points: It predicted proximity across brain regions and spatial technologies, including zero-shot cross-technology transfer.
Inferred neighbourhoods recovered reproducible tissue organisation in datasets with known coordinates.
In an Alzheimer dataset it found age-associated neighbourhood remodelling, including an AD-associated neighbourhood at 8 months.

posts.title: Vizitig: context-rich exploration of sequencing datasets
posts.authors: Degardins B, Paperman C, Marchet C, et al.
posts.summary: Vizitig is a platform for real-time exploration and querying of DNA and RNA compacted colored de Bruijn graphs across many samples, with a metadata-aware query language and on-demand subgraph loading.
key_points: Pantranscriptomic case study: it recovers fusion transcript breakpoints in long and short reads.
Pangenomic case studies span yeast, rice, nematode and human pangenomes.
It scales from small virus genomes to up to 20 assembled human haplotypes on a laptop.

posts.title: Deciphering the Network Architecture of APOBEC3-Driven Mutagenesis in HPV-Positive Head and Neck Cancers
posts.authors: Lehle JD, Soleimanpour M, Haghjoo N, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell profiling of HPV16-positive head and neck tumours and matched normal tissue separates the effects of APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B, which bulk sequencing averages together.
key_points: The APOBEC3 signature SBS2 is enriched in cells expressing more A3A than A3B, while copy number alteration burden is enriched in cells with more A3B than A3A.
Co-expression networks nominate RALY and HNRNPA2B1 as candidate A3 activators.
The SBS2 to CNA ratio may estimate tumour age, and neoantigens from SBS2-high and CNA-high cells suggest mRNA vaccine candidates.

posts.title: Multimodal spatial-omics reveal the heterogeneity and intercellular network characteristics of papillary craniopharyngiomas
posts.authors: Jiang Y, Luo H, Zheng H, et al.
posts.summary: Integrated single-cell and spatial profiling of papillary craniopharyngioma tissue and blood builds a cell-state, spatial and microenvironment atlas of this tumour.
key_points: Four tumour cell states were defined, each with specific transcriptional regulatory programs and spatial features.
A spatial niche of tumour, immune and stromal cells was used to infer cell-cell communication.

posts.title: TET loss of function selects for aneuploidies that confer a proliferative advantage
posts.authors: Lopez-Moyado IF, Suzuki K, Hernandez-Espinosa L, et al.
posts.summary: Loss of Tet2/3 in iNKT cells drives lymphoid expansion consistently tied to chromosome 17 trisomy, suggesting TET loss promotes selection of cryptic aneuploid subclones.
key_points: Single-cell whole-genome sequencing showed rare trisomy 17 cells appear early after Tet deletion and are then progressively enriched.
Tet-deficient mouse embryonic stem cells also selected pre-existing aneuploid states, including trisomy 6.
Reanalysis of Dnmt3a-deficient mouse lymphomas found recurrent chromosome gains including trisomy 17.

posts.title: MOD-scTWAS: Leveraging gene co-expression for single-cell transcriptome-wide association studies
posts.authors: Guo H, Lu Y, Hou L, et al.
posts.summary: MOD-scTWAS jointly models genetically regulated expression for genes inside co-expression modules, borrowing information across genes to improve cell-type-specific TWAS.
key_points: In OneK1K cross-validation it beat scTWAS in mean GReX prediction accuracy across all 14 cell types and imputed more genes.
On UK Biobank haematological traits it found more significant cell type-gene-trait associations than scTWAS.

posts.title: Mendel, a foundation model of human genetic variation, prioritizes regulatory variants and improves gene expression prediction
posts.authors: Salman A, Feng H, Wei P, et al.
posts.summary: Mendel is a DNA foundation model trained from scratch on human whole-genome sequences with a variant-centric objective, so supervision concentrates on allelic events rather than conserved background.
key_points: On held-out individuals it reached 0.984 micro-averaged SNV allele-prediction accuracy versus 0.311 for Evo 2.
Its residual difficulty is enriched at cis-eQTL variants and prioritizes fine-mapped causal variants (AUROC 0.731), where Evo 2 was near chance.
Used as a cis-expression prior, it improved expression prediction in all 50 GTEx tissues.

posts.title: Cell-of-origin shapes tumor subtype in BRCA1-associated triple-negative breast cancer
posts.authors: Lev T, Samy ALPA, Mallya S, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq of 67,001 cells from Wap-Cre Brca1/p53 mice, plus reanalysis of Blg-Cre data, shows triple-negative breast cancer also arises from basal-myoepithelial cells, and that the cell of origin shapes the subtype.
key_points: Aberrant basal-myoepithelial differentiation gives the mesenchymal subtype (TNBC-M); aberrant luminal differentiation gives the basal-like subtype (TNBC-BL1).
Both subtypes occur at comparable frequency in BRCA1 carriers.
Findings argue for including basal-myoepithelial and luminal cells in prevention strategies for BRCA1 carriers.

posts.title: A heritability-optimized method for functional prioritization of rare coding variants in complex traits
posts.authors: Pang K, Pathan N, Le A, et al.
posts.summary: RovHer scores missense rare variants by their probability of being functional, defined as their contribution to trait variance. It uses exome-wide association statistics across 4.9 million rare variants and multivariate adaptive regression splines to combine 75 variant- and gene-level features.
key_points: Across 21 UK Biobank traits (up to 357,086 people), the top 1% of RovHer-ranked variants explained on average 16.1% of rare-variant heritability, about 10-fold more than 7 other methods.
Predictions are independent of allele frequency and replicate in a multi-ancestry analysis.
The scores pick out high-risk carriers of severe outcomes across 17 monogenic gene-trait pairs.

figure.caption: RovHer sifts millions of rare missense variants into a top 1% that carries much of the rare-variant heritability and flags high-risk carriers.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Resolving cell-cell interaction networks and their molecular logic in complex tissues
posts.authors: Tang L, Tian K, Fu X, et al.
posts.summary: CCI-seq captures cell-cell interactions at scale by combining cell clump combinatorial indexing with single-cell sequencing. Because it sits on a single-cell RNA-seq backbone, each interacting cell also gets a full transcriptome, so the molecular state tied to an interaction can be read out.
key_points: It recovered known interactions and fine-grained organisation in mouse kidney and intestine, and showed disrupted interactions in Apc-KO intestines.
In human colorectal cancer it revealed subtype-specific interactions linked to clinical classifications.
Interacting cells carried distinct programmes: ion transport in kidney, antigen presentation in Apc-KO villi and NF-κB inflammatory activation in colorectal cancer.

figure.caption: Touching cells are kept as clumps, barcoded combinatorially and sequenced, giving an interaction network plus each cell's transcriptome.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Global and specific mechanisms stimulate mistranslation in cancer
posts.authors: Wernaart D, Fumagalli A, Adhikary M, et al.
posts.summary: Tryptophan shortage imposed by anti-tumour immunity makes cancer cells mistranslate tryptophan codons, by frameshifting or by reading them as phenylalanine (W>F substitutants). A genetic screen after interferon-γ-driven tryptophan depletion found what controls the W>F events.
key_points: The screen identified ADAR1, an A-to-I RNA editing enzyme, which sustains ribosome quality control pathway genes that are needed for mistranslation.
FTSJ1 2'-O-methylates the anticodon of tRNA-Trp, which promotes its binding to WARS1 loaded with phenylalanine and so drives W>F mistranslation.
ADAR1 and FTSJ1 are elevated in many cancer types, suggesting a general mechanism.

figure.caption: Under tryptophan shortage the ribosome can insert phenylalanine at UGG codons; ADAR1 and FTSJ1 are the screen hits that control this.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Imputation of fluid intelligence scores reduces ascertainment bias and increases power for analyses of common and rare variants
posts.authors: van den Berg DM, Malawsky DS, Huang W, et al.
posts.summary: The authors combined fluid intelligence tests across UK Biobank measures and imputed the score for unmeasured people, raising the sample from about 270,000 to over 455,000. Analyses use only existing biobank data, so it counts as computational.
key_points: The imputed phenotype resembles measured fluid intelligence genetically, though some non-cognitive signal likely remains.
Common-variant hits rose from 390 to 550, and the extra people reduce the bias from test-takers being more educated.
Rare-variant analysis found 26 genes (FDR below 1%), 8 without strong prior links to intelligence, which replicate in aggregate in external cohorts.

posts.title: Function-preserving watermarking of AI-generated proteins
posts.authors: Stutz D, Cowen-Rivers AI, Ortiz-Jimenez G, et al.
posts.summary: SynthIDBio is a family of methods for watermarking protein sequences and structures so AI-generated proteins can be traced to their source. It is posted because Tier 1 journals are tracked for computational biology work, although protein design is otherwise outside the interest list.
key_points: SynthIDBio-sequence embeds a watermark into protein sequences while preserving function; watermarked designed binders had binding affinity comparable with unwatermarked ones, with near-perfect detection.
SynthIDBio-structure is a fine-tuned AlphaFold 3 model that embeds an imperceptible watermark into biomolecular structures.
The authors present it as a proof of concept for provenance and biosecurity.

posts.title: DND1-NANOS3 shapes the PGC transcriptome via a heptanucleotide sequence in mRNA 3' UTRs
posts.authors: Suzawa M, Qiu C, Polash AH, et al.
posts.summary: Primordial germ cell survival needs the RNA-binding proteins DND1 and NANOS3. This study shows they act as a pair, where neither alone has strong sequence specificity, to repress mRNAs through one high-information motif in 3' UTRs.
key_points: Tandem PAR-CLIP showed the DND1-NANOS3 complex represses dozens of epigenome and cell-cycle regulator mRNAs by recognising the heptamer AUGAAUU.
Genome editing of the element relieved repression of CDK1 in vivo.
A structure shows a continuous RNA-binding surface formed by both proteins, and a NANOS3 disordered region adds affinity and specificity.

posts.title: Decoding epithelial-mesenchymal transitions with multi-omics
posts.authors: Narwade N, Nieto MA
posts.summary: A review of how single-cell and spatial omics and computational frameworks such as machine learning and network modelling have advanced the study of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), a plastic programme co-opted in cancer and fibrosis.
key_points: EMT is a continuum of intermediate states, which has limited systematic study across the transcriptome, epigenome, proteome and metabolome.
The review covers analytical considerations, current challenges, and prospects for biomarker discovery and translation.

posts.title: Weighted sliced inverse regression for scalable supervised dimensionality reduction of spatial transcriptomics data
posts.authors: Woollard M, Panwar P, Harland LTG, et al.
posts.summary: wSIR is a supervised dimension-reduction method for spatial transcriptomics that keeps the predictive power of the spatial coordinates, which common variance-preserving reductions do not.
key_points: Works across several spatial platforms and processes over 100,000 cells in under two minutes on a standard laptop.
Feature loadings are interpretable and new non-spatial data can be projected into the same space.
Case studies in human breast cancer and mouse early embryo show biological relevance.

posts.title: Microenvironment-aware transcriptome reconstruction in spatial transcriptomics
posts.authors: Yang ST, Peng P, He HF, et al.
posts.summary: Emerge extends imaging-based spatial transcriptomics, which measures only a gene panel, to transcriptome scale by combining a cell's transcriptional identity with its local microenvironment.
key_points: Local microenvironment explains transcriptional variation beyond cell identity.
Tested on MERFISH and Xenium data from neural and tumour tissue, it improved recovery of structured variation.
It also reveals links among cell states, niches and intercellular communication programmes.

posts.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals laminar and cell-type-specific A-to-I RNA editing signatures in the macaque cortex
posts.authors: Chen C, Yang J, Zhu Z, et al.
posts.summary: The authors built SRDRE, an analysis framework to call RNA editing sites in spatial transcriptomics data, and applied it to over 40 million cells across 142 annotated regions of the adult macaque cortex.
key_points: Editing levels in neurons tracked cortical hierarchy in the visual and somatosensory systems.
Parvalbumin neurons had the highest editing activity in most regions, and primate-enriched sites fell in ion channel genes of prefrontal excitatory neurons.
An exploratory analysis found altered editing in deeper dorsolateral prefrontal layers of macaques with depressive-like behaviour.

posts.title: A systematic single-cell analysis of enhancer RNAs across human and mouse
posts.authors: Rong H, Liu H, Li Y, et al.
posts.summary: Using 187 full-length single-cell RNA-seq datasets (184,329 cells), the study catalogues enhancer RNAs (eRNAs) at single-cell resolution and builds a resource of their expression and regulatory networks.
key_points: Identified 85,977 human and 82,727 mouse eRNAs, sparsely detected per cell but heterogeneous between cells.
eRNAs made up to 33.5% of human and 46.5% of mouse lineage markers.
RACE confirmed a colorectal cancer-associated eRNA whose plasma level supports a possible non-invasive biomarker.

posts.title: CellART: a unified framework for extracting single-cell information from high-resolution spatial transcriptomics
posts.authors: Chen Y, Liu Y, Wang Z, et al.
posts.summary: CellART does cell segmentation and cell-type annotation together for high-resolution spatial transcriptomics, using staining images, the spatial data and a single-cell RNA-seq reference, with deep learning and probabilistic modelling.
key_points: Designed to work across diverse sub-cellular-resolution platforms, including sparse-count and limited-gene-panel ones.
Its outputs are compatible with widely used community tools for downstream analysis.

posts.title: MAJEC: unified gene, isoform, and locus-level transposable element quantification from RNA-seq
posts.authors: Lim TY, Firestone AJ
posts.summary: MAJEC is an expectation-maximisation framework that jointly quantifies genes, transcript isoforms and individual transposable element loci from alignments in one pass, using splice junctions to separate gene reads from TE-derived reads.
key_points: It cuts exon-overlap contamination of locus-level TE estimates from 43% of signal (Telescope) to 5%.
Subfamily-level accuracy is kept (differential expression r = 0.987 vs TEtranscripts), isoform quantification was checked against Salmon and RSEM, and it runs faster than either TE tool.
Examples show it avoids both false TE reactivation and false gene upregulation.

posts.title: Fast and accurate construction of multiple sequence alignments from protein language embeddings with ARIES
posts.authors: Hoang M, Armour-Garb I, Singh M
posts.summary: ARIES builds multiple sequence alignments from protein language model embeddings: it makes a template embedding and aligns every sequence to it by dynamic time warping. The aim is better accuracy in the low-identity twilight zone.
key_points: A windowed reciprocal-weighted embedding similarity identifies corresponding amino acids across sequences.
Across benchmarks it beats state-of-the-art aligners, especially at low identity, and scales almost linearly with sequence number.

posts.title: Scaling coalescent-based species tree inference to 100,000 taxa with STELAR-X
posts.authors: Saha A, Bayzid MS
posts.summary: STELAR-X is a statistically consistent, triplet-based species tree method that uses a compact tuple encoding of bipartitions, precomputed weights and GPU parallelism to scale far beyond ASTRAL and STELAR.
key_points: On 10,000 taxa and 1,000 gene trees it ran 3,576 times faster than ASTRAL-MP with 13.9 times less memory.
It analysed 100,000 taxa with 1,000 genes in about 34 minutes, and trees for two avian datasets matched established bird phylogenies.

posts.title: Functional roles for viral RNA ribosylation in mammalian cells
posts.authors: Sears JD, Chang CK, Shirasaki T, et al.
posts.summary: During chikungunya virus infection, viral RNA is ribosylated by the PARP12 ribosyltransferase and counteracted by the viral nsP3 macrodomain hydrolase. The study asks what ribosylation does to RNA.
key_points: Ribosylated RNA was translated less in cell-free systems and infected fibroblasts, and viral RNA decayed faster.
Ribosylated RNA strongly induced antiviral host response genes, so it acts like a pathogen-associated molecular pattern.
Because macrodomains occur in many unrelated viruses, RNA ribosylation may be a general part of antiviral sensing.

posts.title: Determining gene specificity from multivariate single-cell RNA sequencing data
posts.authors: Swarna NP, Booeshaghi AS, Rebboah E, et al.
posts.summary: ember is an entropy-based framework that scores how specific a gene is to biological categories in single-cell data, using Shannon's chain rule across nested partitions. It is applied to eight tissues from eight founder mouse strains and a 255-person PBMC dataset.
key_points: Gene specificity is often unintuitive: canonical markers can be supplanted and housekeeping genes are context-dependent.
In PBMCs, variation is largely localised to classical monocytes, with genes of unique specificity by sex, age and ancestry.
A specificity database with web interface, API and MCP server is provided.

posts.title: GBZ-base and GAF-base: Indexed pangenome file formats
posts.authors: Siren J, Paten B, Human Pangenome Reference Consortium
posts.summary: GBZ-base and GAF-base are SQLite-backed pangenome file formats that can be queried directly from disk, unlike existing formats built for batch processing in memory.
key_points: GBZ-base supports efficient extraction of local subgraphs and GAF-base extracts all alignments to a subgraph.
GAF-base is smaller than any other format for sequence-to-graph alignments.

posts.title: EpiZoo: a DNA sequence-aware foundation model for cross-species single-cell epigenomics
posts.authors: Li K, Chen X, Jiang Q, et al.
posts.summary: EpiZoo is a 2.6-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts transformer pretrained on about 20.9 million single-cell ATAC cells from many species. It encodes DNA sequence into cell 'sentences', so it does not depend on genomic coordinates.
key_points: Reports state-of-the-art feature extraction, cell type annotation and imputation on datasets held out of pretraining.
Supports comparison of regulatory conservation across primates, prioritisation of somatic mutations in cancer, and prediction of accessibility from sequence.

posts.title: SpatialTRACE predicts anatomical axes and regions in spatial transcriptomics and microscopy
posts.authors: Monell AT, Gogate AA, Patravali D, et al.
posts.summary: SpatialTRACE extends a few annotated structures into tissue-wide maps of anatomical axes and regions. A graph model uses expression plus spatial neighbourhoods; an image model learns from it to predict the same coordinates from DAPI alone.
key_points: In held-out mouse small-intestine sections the graph model predicted crypt-villus axis coordinates with as few as 10 annotated villi and found Peyer's patches.
Applied to immunofluorescence, it mapped where antigen-specific CD8 T cells sit in the intestine after LCMV infection.

posts.title: Platform-specific count-matrix preprocessing workflows for spatial transcriptomics data analysis
posts.authors: Du Y, Li S, Yang X, et al.
posts.summary: A benchmark of 371 count-matrix preprocessing workflows on 45 datasets from 11 spatial transcriptomics platforms, plus image preprocessing steps such as cell segmentation.
key_points: No single workflow was best across platforms, but data from the same platform favoured the same workflows.
The authors give platform- and data-structure-guided recommendations, and show the best choice uncovers spatial patterns hidden by poor preprocessing.

posts.title: Distinct sequence grammars of nucleosomal and linker DNA shape mutational and methylation landscapes in cancer
posts.authors: Masoudi-Sobhanzadeh Y, Kumar S
posts.summary: DeepND is an interpretable deep learning model that separates nucleosomal from inter-nucleosomal DNA and reveals the sequence motifs behind it, then links them to somatic mutations and DNA methylation in cancer.
key_points: 210 motifs of 2-16 bp were enriched or depleted in nucleosomal DNA; 44 had cancer-type-specific mutation patterns and 6 were tied to methylation differences.
Mutations in lung and endometrial cancers showed a roughly 10-bp periodic pattern linked to minor-groove orientation.

posts.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals tumour cell-intrinsic and microenvironmental features associated with survival in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma
posts.authors: Khan MAAK, Lin W, Denisenko E, et al.
posts.summary: Xenium spatial transcriptomics with a custom 480-gene panel was applied to treatment-naive tumours from 122 high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma patients, to separate tumour-cell from microenvironment signals linked to survival.
key_points: 61 tumour-intrinsic genes were nominally tied to overall survival, and 46 of them were not significant when expression was pooled over all cells in a patient.
Immune populations near tumour cells were linked to longer survival and two fibroblast populations to shorter survival.
Consensus clustering gave four patient groups with different tumour-intrinsic and microenvironment combinations.

posts.title: Matched primary-metastasis single-nucleus and spatial profiling of leiomyosarcoma identifies antigen-presenting fibroblasts at the tumor-organ interface
posts.authors: Kuebler A, Bergmayr L, Knoesel T, et al.
posts.summary: Single-nucleus RNA-seq of four matched primary-metastasis leiomyosarcoma pairs (from archival FFPE tissue) was combined with spatial transcriptomics of 21 patients, with malignant cells defined by inferred copy number and checked against DNA methylation.
key_points: Malignant programmes were organ-associated: stress and hypoxia in lung metastases, proliferative matrix remodelling in liver metastases.
Antigen-presenting fibroblasts were enriched in metastases and formed a band at the tumour-organ interface.
Three histomolecular phenotypes were resolved, including a GPNMB one that might be targetable.

posts.title: A generative language model decodes contextual constraints on codon choice for mRNA design
posts.authors: Faizi M, Sakharova H, Lareau LF
posts.summary: Trias is a generative encoder-decoder language model trained on millions of vertebrate coding sequences to learn codon usage rules, used to design mRNAs with high protein output. This is a later version (v3) of a preprint first posted in May 2025.
key_points: Zero-shot predictions correlate strongly with measured mRNA stability and protein output, without training on expression.
Experimentally, Trias-designed sequences for a therapeutic target gave more protein than existing methods.
Open-source code and weights are released.

posts.title: Pangenome-resolved polymorphic transposable elements reveal human regulatory evolution in action
posts.authors: Jiang J, Zhuo X, Li R, et al.
posts.summary: Using 231 haplotype-resolved human pangenomes with matched long-read multi-omics, segregating transposable element alleles are resolved as sequences, epigenetic states and transcript components.
key_points: Regulatory effects depend on methylation and transcript context and are often missed by gene-level analyses.
The elements give mechanisms at trait-associated loci, and selection favours both presence and absence of elements.

posts.title: En Bloc Resection for Primary Malignant Tumors of the Subaxial Cervical Spine: Oncologic and Technical Considerations
posts.authors: Benato A, Du R, Kemeny H, et al.
posts.summary: Four illustrative cases and a narrative review set out how en bloc resection is planned and carried out for primary malignant bone tumours of the subaxial cervical spine, with a stepwise framework for surgical decisions. PubMed returned it for a chordoma search, but the abstract text retrieved did not name chordoma, so it is posted as a mixed spine-tumour series.
key_points: Success depends on assessing tumour histology, compartmental extension, vertebral artery involvement, epidural disease and relations to the brachial plexus.
Multistage circumferential approaches are often needed to set osteotomy planes and restore spinal stability.
When en bloc resection is not feasible, stabilisation, decompression and radiation therapy are combined; larger prospective series are needed.

posts.title: Inferring gene expression profiles of tumor clones
posts.authors: Shafighi S, Jurzysta B, Szczurek E
posts.summary: CLONALGE is a probabilistic graphical model that finds cancer clone genotypes, their gene expression profiles and their positions in tissue. It matches single-nucleotide variant sites seen in spatial transcriptomics to clone-specific variants from DNA sequencing and deconvolves each spot into clone contributions.
key_points: A Monte Carlo procedure with a HDI+ROPE criterion picks genes that differ between clones.
It fills a gap: tools that infer clone genotypes and transcriptional phenotypes together in tumour tissue were lacking.

posts.title: Quantifying distribution shifts in single-cell data with scXMatch
posts.authors: Möller A, Schnitzerlein M, Greto E, et al.
posts.summary: scXMatch is a non-parametric, graph-based test that quantifies whether cells from two conditions differ globally in any space with a usable distance. It aims to replace visual inspection of embeddings and clustering-based workflows, which are unstable and prone to confirmation bias.
key_points: Tested on single-cell gene expression, chromatin accessibility and imaging-derived cell morphology data.
The authors report that it robustly detects distribution shifts across these data types; Python code is available.

posts.title: SingPro 2.0: a proteomics-centric knowledge base for single-cell multimodal profiling
posts.authors: Zhou Y, Deng J, Zhu Z, et al.
posts.summary: SingPro was expanded from a single-cell proteomics database into a knowledge base of protein-inclusive single-cell multimodal studies. It curates data and experimental details from 814 studies covering about 81.5 million cells.
key_points: Covers 29 tissues, 44 diseases and several species, across 5 omics modalities and 12 technologies.
Offers cross-modality visualisation for joint analysis; free to use without login.

posts.title: GROMTools: scalable individual-level GReX imputation for mega-biobank-scale cohorts
posts.authors: Anyfantakis M, Venkatesh S, Bennett JJR, et al.
posts.summary: GROMTools is an open-source C++ engine with an R interface for imputing genetically regulated gene expression (GReX) at individual level in mega-biobanks. It uses sparse prediction weights and streams PLINK2 genotypes to cut runtime and memory.
key_points: In UK Biobank benchmarks (up to 450,000 individuals, 32 single-nucleus imputation models) predictions matched PrediXcan and PLINK2 (Pearson correlation above 0.999).
CPU time fell about 10-fold and peak memory about 33-fold.

posts.title: DiCE-Ex: a web server for network-based differential-centrality gene exploration
posts.authors: Lokuge SD, Liu S, Shang M, et al.
posts.summary: DiCE-Ex is a web server that ranks genes by how much their network role changes between conditions. It combines expression data with protein-protein interaction networks and compares an ensemble of centrality measures, so it can surface regulators without large expression changes.
key_points: Case studies recovered known disease modulators and also flagged non-hub regulators that differential expression missed.
Freely available with example data and tutorials.

posts.title: Systematic transcriptomic evaluation of blastoid models of early human development
posts.authors: Long S, Kim HJ, Salehin N, et al.
posts.summary: The authors built a reference map of human blastocyst cell identities by integrating single-cell transcriptomes of ex vivo blastocysts across culture time points. They used it to judge how well different stem-cell-derived blastoid models cover and match real blastocyst lineages.
key_points: The reference map benchmarks lineage coverage, authenticity and progression of differentiation across blastoid protocols.
It is meant to guide optimisation of higher-fidelity blastoid models.

posts.title: Dynamic tRNA modification programs align codon usage with growth-phase-specific gene expression in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
posts.authors: Frommeyer YN, Sun J, Wu J, et al.
posts.summary: Time-resolved nanopore tRNA sequencing, LC-MS/MS modification profiling, transcriptomics and proteomics across the PA14 growth cycle show tRNA-modifying enzymes, their modifications and dependent genes expressed in a coordinated temporal cascade.
key_points: GidA-dependent mnm5s2U rises after GidA expression peaks, coinciding with peak expression of genes rich in rare AGA and UUA codons and with virulence-associated functions.
The pattern may help horizontally acquired genes bridge codon-usage differences with the core genome.

posts.title: Optical genome mapping identifies clinically relevant somatic structural variation in epilepsy-affected brain tissue
posts.authors: Miller AR, Anderson JJ, Hernandez Gonzalez ME, et al.
posts.summary: The authors optimised optical genome mapping (OGM) for surgically resected brain tissue, reaching about 450x effective coverage, and applied it to four patients with epilepsy-associated cortical malformations. OGM found large and complex somatic structural variants that exome sequencing mostly missed.
key_points: In one patient with a known germline variant, OGM revealed a somatic 13.2 kb deletion at about 20% allele fraction, fitting a two-hit model.
PacBio HiFi data resolved the breakpoints and pointed to recombination between two flanking elements.

posts.title: Single-cell spatial mapping reveals reproducible cell type organization and spatially dependent gene expression in gastruloids
posts.authors: Triandafillou C, Sompalle P, Heyman Y, et al.
posts.summary: The authors made a spatially resolved single-cell transcriptome catalogue of 26 individual gastruloids. Cell-type composition and tissue-scale organisation were largely consistent, while meso-scale patterning of particular cell types varied between samples.
key_points: They developed the L-score, a parameter-free measure of mutually exclusive gene expression that separates progressive differentiation from cell-type differences.
Neuromesodermal precursors differentiated in a continuous, spatially coordinated way; endothelial precursors showed distinct spatial organisation.

posts.title: Cooperativity through Allee Effects drives growth of diffuse midline gliomas impacting the optimal scheduling of therapeutic interventions
posts.authors: Tari H, Kessler K, Izquierdo E, et al.
posts.summary: The authors extend the Lotka-Volterra competition model to show that subpopulations from the same diffuse midline glioma can interact through Allee effects. Therapy perturbs these interactions, which changes the simulated outcome of treatment schedules.
key_points: Interactions between subpopulations can offset the effect of therapy.
In a simulated two-drug regimen, the interactions substantially changed outcomes depending on scheduling.

posts.title: Multi-scale Transcriptional Characterization of HPV16 and HPV18 in Cervical Cancer: Host Pathway Alterations and Links With Viral Gene Expression Programs
posts.authors: Ishihara MA, Moro Valeriano MM, Oliveira N, et al.
posts.summary: Using viral and host RNA data from two cervical cancer cohorts (n = 93; 76 HPV16, 17 HPV18), the authors show the two genotypes differ in host transcriptional programs. A 55-gene signature separates them, and 293 genes were concordantly differential across cohorts.
key_points: HPV16 tumours were enriched for epithelial polarity and RTK-RAS-MAPK signatures, with inferred CDX2 regulon activity.
HPV18 tumours showed metabolic and inflammatory (STAT3, HIF1A) programs, lower CASP8 and higher FDX1.
Viral early-to-late gene expression correlated with distinct host pathways in each genotype.

posts.title: Transcriptomic analysis reveals differential regulation of synaptic components in pediatric and adult brain tumors
posts.authors: Merino-Galan L, Arora S, Glatzer G, et al.
posts.summary: The authors assembled a reference map from bulk RNA-seq of about 4,300 adult and paediatric brain tumours and about 1,400 healthy brain samples, and used it to examine synaptic gene expression across tumour types.
key_points: HNRNPH2, an RNA processing factor, is upregulated in gliomas and medulloblastomas.
CHRNA9 (cholinergic signalling) is proposed as a driver of glioma progression and is also raised in WNT and Group 4 medulloblastomas, ependymomas and meningiomas.
P2 purinergic signalling also emerges as a player in glioma progression.

posts.title: Integrated transcriptomic analysis identifies Paternally Expressed Gene 10 as a novel candidate biomarker associated with aggressive features in liposarcoma
posts.authors: Turiello R, Scognamiglio G, Bonicelli A, et al.
posts.summary: Bulk RNA-seq of paired liposarcoma and adjacent normal tissue (16 patients) showed subtype-specific programs and broad dysregulation of imprinted genes. PEG10 stood out as a candidate biomarker of aggressive disease.
key_points: PEG10 separated tumour from normal tissue in the discovery cohort (AUC 0.867) and was higher in high-grade tumours.
High PEG10 was linked to shorter overall survival in TCGA-SARC and to reduced immune infiltration in an external single-cell dataset.
The authors say validation in larger, subtype-balanced cohorts is needed.

posts.title: Stochastically Emergent Tumors offer in vivo whole genome interrogation of cancer evolution from non-malignant precursors
posts.authors: Moussavi-Baygi R, Ryan MJ, Sim W, et al.
posts.summary: Stochastically Emergent Tumors (SETs) are an in vivo platform in which tumours evolve through combinatorial genome-wide alterations without chromosomal instability, giving sparse genetic variation suited to computational inference and deep learning. Applied to prostate cancer under hormone therapy, they reveal what shapes sensitivity and resistance.
key_points: Six previously unrecognised sensitisation determinants were found, including ZFHX3 loss; CIC and KMT2D alterations were linked to resistance.
Patient tumour analyses tied these candidates to clinical outcomes, and ZFHX3 was nominated as a target to push tumours into a luminal state.

posts.title: Sex-specific differences in ADAR editing patterns in response to SARS-CoV-2 infections
posts.authors: Nair AM, Piontkivska H
posts.summary: Re-analysing a public whole-blood RNA-seq dataset matched for age and comorbidity, the authors compare ADAR expression and A-to-I editing between sexes before, during and after SARS-CoV-2 infection.
key_points: ADAR and ADAR2 expression differed by sex pre- and mid-infection but not after clearance; ADAR3 was higher in females mid-infection.
The ADAR expression to global editing relationship differed by sex and stage, so editing is not set by transcript abundance alone.
Editing within genes that escape X-inactivation differed at baseline and across infection stages independently of expression.

posts.title: Limitations of differential expression for cell-type marker discovery in single-cell RNA sequencing atlases
posts.authors: Doggett K, Pintard D, Scheuermann RH, et al.
posts.summary: The authors show that the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, the default for marker discovery in Seurat and recommended in Scanpy, gives scores that grow with cluster size, so rankings across unequal clusters are not comparable. They tested this on lung, kidney and brain atlases.
key_points: Mean Wilcoxon score correlated with log cluster size at r = 0.90-0.95, versus r = 0.10-0.28 for the classification-based NS-Forest.
Normalising to a rank-based effect size removes the size dependence but nominates the same genes, so poor specificity is a separate problem.
Median on-target fraction of default DE markers was 0.083-0.204, versus 0.364-0.687 for NS-Forest.

posts.title: Trustworthy super-resolution reconstruction across spatial omics modalities
posts.authors: Li M, Wang X, Xu S, et al.
posts.summary: spEnhance reconstructs high-resolution spatial molecular profiles from spot-level spatial omics data by combining histology features with single-cell RNA-seq references and gene co-expression structure. It adds a count-splitting scheme to validate and select models from a single tissue section.
key_points: Predictive residuals give a spatial reliability estimate for each prediction.
Benchmarks across tissues, platforms and modalities show state-of-the-art accuracy and less overfitting.
It extends beyond transcriptomics to isoform-level, epigenomic, proteomic and metabolomic spatial data.

posts.title: Paired plus-minus sequencing is an ultra-high throughput and accurate method for dual strand sequencing of DNA molecules
posts.authors: Cheng AP, Rusinek I, Sossin A, et al.
posts.summary: Paired plus-minus sequencing (ppmSeq) clonally amplifies both strands of a DNA molecule on one bead so a single read carries duplex information. This gives duplex recovery that scales with coverage, aimed at low-frequency variant settings such as ctDNA and somatic mosaicism.
key_points: Duplex recovery was 44% +/- 5.5%, versus about 5-11% for leading duplex technologies; residual SNV error was as low as 7.98x10^-8 for gDNA.
Tumour-informed ctDNA detection reached 10^-4 concentrations across most cancers, and mutation-signature-based tumour-naive detection worked in urothelial and lung cancers.

posts.title: Spatially resolved multiomics of human meningeal development reveal lineage and disease dynamics
posts.authors: To K, Pett JP, Dufva O, et al.
posts.summary: The authors built a paired single-nucleus RNA and ATAC atlas of the human meninges from 6 to 21 weeks of gestation and added spatial transcriptomics to place cell types in the meningeal layers. The atlas defines the regulatory networks behind blood-brain barrier endothelium and points to a yolk sac origin for meningeal myeloid cells.
key_points: They release two tools: Nichefinder for spatial label transfer and proximity analysis, and cell2home for inferring chemotactic signalling.
cell2home suggests interactions that could draw B cells from cranial marrow into the prenatal meninges.
In trisomy 21, meningeal fibroblasts show lower chemokine expression and stronger JAK-STAT signalling.

figure.caption: Human meninges: a marrow-to-meninges B-cell route, a yolk sac origin for macrophages, and weaker chemokine with stronger JAK-STAT signalling in trisomy 21 fibroblasts.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: A human single-cell atlas identifies OLR1scar-associated macrophages as a potential therapeutic target for chronic liver disease
posts.authors: Papachristoforou E, Kong K, Colella F, et al.
posts.summary: The authors assembled a liver single-cell atlas of 649,295 cells from 42 healthy people and 35 people with chronic liver disease, covering 125 cell states. It separates two disease-expanded TREM2+ scar-associated macrophage types, including a pro-inflammatory OLR1+ type found in the fibrotic niche.
key_points: High liver OLR1 expression tracks with more fibrosis across disease causes and with worse outcomes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
OLR1+ macrophages also expand in a mouse model, and targeting macrophage OLR1 lowered fibrogenic activity in human co-culture and spheroid models.
The atlas is offered as a reference for disease-associated cell states in chronic liver disease.

figure.caption: Healthy liver compared with fibrotic liver, where TREM2+ and pro-inflammatory OLR1+ scar-associated macrophages sit in the fibrotic niche.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: CSGDA: A Cell State-Guided Graph Domain Adaptation Network for Single-Cell Drug Response Prediction
posts.authors: Yan F, Xie D, Cao X, et al.
posts.summary: CSGDA predicts single-cell drug response when the training and target data differ, for example from cell lines to tissue or from primary to metastatic tumours. It maps gene expression into functional cell states and uses graph domain adaptation with an overlap penalty to cope with the shift.
key_points: On five scRNA-seq datasets it beat the previous best method SSDA4Drug by about 6 percentage points in accuracy and AUPR.
Integrated gradients on a cross-metastasis cisplatin dataset highlighted genes linked to drug resistance.

posts.title: scURL: Uncertainty-Sharpened Representation Learning for Single-cell Multi-omics Clustering
posts.authors: Liu H, Yu D, Li W, et al.
posts.summary: scURL clusters single-cell multi-omics data while estimating how reliable each omics layer is for each cell. It turns that uncertainty into cell-wise weights for fusing the layers and calibrates each layer before fusion.
key_points: It outperformed existing clustering methods on ten datasets.
It stayed robust under dropout noise and found cell populations supported by marker genes.

posts.title: RAGCell: Retrieval-Augmented Generation as Supervision for Versatile Single-cell Analysis
posts.authors: Liu T, Zhang F, Chen J, et al.
posts.summary: RAGCell is a single-cell analysis framework that uses a language model to build cell-level and feature-level knowledge databases, then aligns cell representations with text embeddings from them. This avoids the heavy pretraining that single-cell foundation models need.
key_points: It was tested on six downstream single-cell tasks.
The authors report performance matching or beating state-of-the-art single-cell foundation models at lower training cost.

posts.title: OrchAlign: Orchestrated Multimodal Alignment for Gene Expression Prediction
posts.authors: Liu L, Xv G, Liu S, et al.
posts.summary: OrchAlign predicts gene expression from DNA sequence and epigenomic signals. Instead of simple concatenation, it aligns the two modalities token by token on a shared representation within a key regulatory region.
key_points: Each modality is split into shared and specific parts, and the aligned parts keep their internal structure through a consistency term.
A BiMamba backbone fuses the representations, and the authors report state-of-the-art gene expression prediction.

posts.title: ScanTCR Enables Early Cancer Detection by Repertoire-Scale Representation of Cancer-Associated T-Cell Receptors in Peripheral Blood
posts.authors: Zhang J, Cai Y, Que J, et al.
posts.summary: ScanTCR is a computational framework that detects cancer early from the T-cell receptor repertoire in peripheral blood. It encodes the whole repertoire against a reference instead of using only high-frequency receptors.
key_points: In a pan-cancer analysis of seven cancer types it separated patients from non-cancer individuals and detected cancer types not seen in training.
It beat existing TCR-based methods and found cancer-associated TCRs whose T cells show stronger immune capacity.

posts.title: Phosphoproteomic dysregulation promotes tumor proliferation in Cushing's disease
posts.authors: Asuzu DT, Bhatt D, Mullaney D, et al.
posts.summary: The authors profiled chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, transcriptome, proteome and phosphoproteome in paired Cushing disease pituitary adenomas and adjacent normal pituitary. In the adenomas, a neurodevelopmental phosphoprotein program that is normally lost after birth is switched back on.
key_points: Adenoma cells overexpress PPP1R17, an inhibitor of the phosphatase PP2A; overexpressing it in normal mouse pituitary cells reproduced the hyperproliferation.
Fingolimod reversed that growth in a PP2A-dependent way in vitro and in vivo.

posts.title: Placenta-Related PEG10 Inhibits mRNA Decay to Promote Glucose Metabolism and Tumor Progression in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
posts.authors: Yao X, Wu B, Yang C, et al.
posts.summary: The authors screened placenta-specific genes that are abnormally expressed in liver cancer and found the retrovirus-like gene PEG10 overexpressed with poor prognosis. PEG10 acts as an RNA-binding protein that blocks Staufen1-mediated mRNA decay.
key_points: Blocking decay stabilises GLUT1 and HK2 mRNAs, raising glucose uptake and glycolysis in tumour cells.
Liver-specific Peg10 deletion slowed hepatocarcinogenesis in mice, and retinoic acid suppressed PEG10 and worked with sorafenib.

posts.title: dioscRi enables transferable prediction of clinical outcomes in multi-parameter cytometry data
posts.authors: Willie E, Rao S, Figtree G, et al.
posts.summary: dioscRi is a deep learning framework for predicting clinical outcomes from multi-parameter cytometry data in a way that transfers across datasets. A variational autoencoder normalises and de-noises the data, and an overlapping group LASSO uses cell type hierarchies.
key_points: It recovered known immune associations in a coronary artery disease study.
It outperformed existing methods on three of four benchmark datasets when moving between cohorts with compatible marker panels.

posts.title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models for aging biology
posts.authors: Ni X, Liang Y, Zhu J, et al.
posts.summary: The authors benchmarked ten general single-cell foundation models, three aging-specific models and conventional methods on five aging questions using more than 2.5 million single-cell transcriptomes. Performance depended on the question.
key_points: Geneformer was best among foundation models for age prediction, though 2,000 highly variable genes scored higher on average.
SCimilarity was best for rare cell state identification, and scGPT recovered the most reference TF targets.

posts.title: NexuST: A Hierarchical Foundation Model for Spatial Transcriptomics
posts.authors: Liu H, Zhao Q, Lin L, et al.
posts.summary: NexuST is a spatial transcriptomics foundation model that alternates gene-level molecular modelling with cell-level spatial modelling during pretraining. It was pretrained on HumanST-46M, 45.7 million human cells from 72 datasets.
key_points: On four held-out datasets (about 2.6 million cells) it was state of the art or competitive for cell-type annotation, region prediction, gene recovery and neighbourhood composition.
An expression-only PCA baseline stayed informative even for spatial tasks.

posts.title: AtlasOT - The Fused Unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein for Multimodal Integration of Disease Atlases
posts.authors: Peng K, Ruiz M, Caron B, et al.
posts.summary: AtlasOT integrates unpaired single-cell and spatial modalities with optimal transport. It maps cells only within the same donor or specimen and allows different cell recovery between modalities.
key_points: It beat baselines on scRNA-scATAC and scRNA-spatial mapping.
The transport plan also helps with rare cell detection, spot-level deconvolution, spatial gene imputation and spatial regulatory dynamics.

posts.title: Mutation Order and Selection Shape Intratumor Heterogeneity in Tumor Evolution
posts.authors: Chu Y, Sheng X, Zhang X, et al.
posts.summary: The authors model a tumour where malignancy needs two driver mutations, acquired in either order, using a multitype branching process. They derive a closed-form expression for clonal concentration (Simpson index).
key_points: A strong driver acquired early increases the supply of independent malignant founders; the same driver acquired last favours the growth of early clones.
Additive fitness can give a non-monotone link between selection and concentration, and threshold-like effects give highly concentrated populations.

posts.title: Unsupervised transcriptomic analysis of paired pre- and post-treatment specimens reveals divergent chemoimmunomodulatory induction trajectories in breast cancer
posts.authors: Lopes de Lima I, Molchan E, Streeks K, et al.
posts.summary: The authors built CIMIC, an unsupervised pipeline that clusters the change in expression of 3,189 immune-related genes between pre- and post-chemotherapy breast tumours. It finds two trajectories, a functional and a dysfunctional one.
key_points: The functional trajectory shows inflammatory cell death, antigen presentation and adaptive immune programs; the dysfunctional one shows stress-adaptation programs and lower cytotoxic activity.
Baseline scores for each trajectory tracked with better or worse outcomes in METABRIC and SCAN-B.

posts.title: Pervasive Somatic Mutations in NF1 Drive Cell Type and Spatially Specific Clonal Selection in Neurofibromatosis
posts.authors: Snellings D, Essuman K, Finander B, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell genomics in more than 1.7 million cells from people with neurofibromatosis type 1 shows that somatic second-hit NF1 mutations are common and positively selected in oligodendrocytes and their precursors, but very rare in neurons.
key_points: Spatial genotyping shows mutant precursor clones expand more in gray matter than white matter.
NF1-null oligodendrocyte lineage cells upregulate CDKN2A, while tumours from the same people lose it, suggesting CDKN2A loss is a key progression step.

posts.title: ctDNA Release Heterogeneity in Luminal Breast Cancer Revealed by Single-Cell Multi-Omics Spatial Analysis
posts.authors: Xu H, Pu P, Liu B, et al.
posts.summary: The authors developed scMASTER, combining single-cell transcriptomes and mutations, spatial transcriptomics and matched tumour and plasma DNA sequencing in ten HR+/HER2- breast cancer patients, to find which tumour cells release ctDNA.
key_points: Eight recurrent malignant states differed in release; antigen-presentation, stress, mitosis and mesenchymal-like states released most.
Three spatial regions (EMT-enriched, intraductal luminal progenitor, hypoxic) released most, and a stratification model was validated in external cohorts.

posts.title: Integrative Nanopore and Illumina sequencing reveals age-associated tRNA modification and CCA-tail dynamics in yeast
posts.authors: Brazell K, Prevost C, Zawrotna N, et al.
posts.summary: The authors present a benchmarked nanopore direct RNA sequencing (RNA004) resource for the yeast tRNAome during replicative aging, validated with Illumina sequencing and in vitro transcribed controls.
key_points: Overall tRNA abundance stays largely stable, but mature tRNAs lose the terminal A of the 3' CCA tail with age.
They also see targeted T-loop and anticodon modification changes and single-molecule co-occurrence of modifications.

posts.title: m6A-Driven Intratumoral Cholesterol Biosynthesis Fuels Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Progression
posts.authors: Lee J, Zhang Z, Hong J, et al.
posts.summary: The authors show that METTL3 interacts with the nucleoporin NUP93 to export m6A-modified mRNAs, and that this is coupled to cholesterol biosynthesis in castration-resistant prostate cancer.
key_points: Overexpressing wild-type METTL3 or NUP93, but not catalytically dead METTL3 or a METTL3-binding-defective NUP93, raised androgen levels and androgen-independent growth.
Inhibiting METTL3 or demethylating cholesterol-enzyme mRNAs suppressed growth.

posts.title: Critical assessment of nanopore sequencing for the detection of multiple forms of DNA modifications
posts.authors: Kong Y, Zhang Y, Mead E, et al.
posts.summary: The authors introduce modFDR, a framework that uses negative controls and false discovery rates to assess nanopore detection of DNA modifications. Detection is reliable for abundant marks but not for rare ones.
key_points: 5mC at CpG sites and 5hmC in brain cells are detected reliably.
Low-abundance marks (5mC at CpH, 5hmC, 6mA) in most mammalian cell types have many false positives, and 5mCpG shows elevated false negatives.

posts.title: An epigenetic program dictates MYC amplification dynamics that promote transient, extrachromosomal, and inherited genomic events
posts.authors: Ferman BI, Azadegan C, Santoro J, et al.
posts.summary: The authors ask how MYC copy gains first arise from a diploid genome. They show that H3K4 methylation primes MYC for amplification by the demethylase KDM4C, while the methyltransferase SETD2 holds copy gains back.
key_points: SETD2 loss or inhibition recruits active KDM4C, which starts and drives stepwise MYC copy gains; the same relationships appear in tumour datasets.
Blocking apoptosis or losing TP53 speeds up higher-level amplification, including extrachromosomal circular DNA and inherited copy gains.
Non-transformed cells with these changes are tumorigenic, and KDM4C inhibition suppresses MYC amplification.

figure.caption: H3K4me-primed MYC is amplified through KDM4C and restrained by SETD2, giving stepwise copy gains that end in ecDNA, sped up by TP53 loss or blocked apoptosis.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Euchromatin forms condensed domains with short active regions on the surface
posts.authors: Paggi JM, Long LY, Zhang B
posts.summary: The authors built a simulation framework that turns region-capture micro-C contact maps into conformational ensembles of megabase-scale regions at nucleosome resolution. The inferred structures contradict the classical view of euchromatin as uniformly open.
key_points: A micro-C balancing step corrects for variation in contact density, and the simulations reproduce distances measured by chromatin tracing.
Euchromatin forms condensed domains of similar density but smaller size than heterochromatin domains.
Kilobase-scale promoters and enhancers often protrude from these domains and become highly accessible, which may help protein binding and enhancer-promoter contact.

figure.caption: Instead of an open fibre, simulated euchromatin forms condensed domains from which promoters and enhancers protrude.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Photolabile oligonucleotides with topological light gradients enable spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomics and epigenomics
posts.authors: Piscopio RA, Chialastri A, Wang C, et al.
posts.summary: scSTAMP-seq labels live or fixed cells with cholesterol-conjugated, photocleavable hashtag oligonucleotides. Patterned light then 'stamps' spatial coordinates onto cells before standard single-cell multiome sequencing.
key_points: Spatial information is kept while using standard single-cell platforms, so no specialised spatial instrument is needed.
The method is modular and works for both transcriptomics and multiome profiling.
Applied to human embryoids, it shows how spatial organisation and epigenetic states jointly regulate cellular programs.

figure.caption: Photocleavable tags on cells are cut by a patterned light gradient, so each cell's position is read out with its RNA and chromatin profile.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Population-scale immune multiome atlas reveals regulatory disease mechanisms
posts.authors: Kanai M, Delorey TM, Honkanen J, et al.
posts.summary: The authors profiled chromatin accessibility and gene expression together in 10 million PBMCs from 1,108 Finnish individuals. The paired data link non-coding variants to disease through chromatin-to-expression cascades.
key_points: They report 51,083 cis-eQTLs, 338,100 cis-chromatin accessibility QTLs, 119,094 putative causal variants and 593,765 peak-gene links.
Variants that complete a chromatin-to-expression cascade show twice the disease colocalisation of chromatin-only effects; 10,428 fine-mapped QTLs were validated by massively parallel reporter assays.
At evolutionarily constrained genes, accessibility changes are buffered before reaching expression, through weaker and more numerous enhancer-gene links.

posts.title: The early RNA decay factor ZC3H18 directs first intron splicing
posts.authors: Le Rest M, El Houda Benbahouche N, Kuhn CC, et al.
posts.summary: The authors show that ZC3H18, known as an early RNA decay linker, also stimulates splicing of the first intron genome-wide. It does this by interacting with the splicing factors PRPF40A, PRP4K and FNBP4.
key_points: Disrupting the CBC-ARS2-ZC3H18 axis corrupts first intron splicing, linking the effect to the cap-binding complex.
ZC3H18's binding to splicing factors is mutually exclusive with its binding to the NEXT decay complex.
The model: splicing factors displace NEXT, sending nascent RNA down a productive splicing path instead of decay.

posts.title: Profiling extracellular vesicle glycoRNAs defines their function in vesicular communication
posts.authors: Chen X, Hao C, Chen X, et al.
posts.summary: The authors show that extracellular vesicles carry glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs). Metabolic tagging with bioorthogonal handles let them enrich and sequence these RNAs and track them by imaging.
key_points: EV glycoRNAs differ by sequence, vesicle type and transfer dynamics; large and small EVs show distinct repertoires.
EVs deliver glycoRNAs to recipient cells, and hybridisation-based blockade of glycoRNAs strongly reduces EV uptake.
The authors suggest EV glycoRNAs are biomarkers of cell state and regulators of vesicle tropism.

posts.title: Lineage identity governs oncogene dependence in mouse NSCLC models of KRAS inhibitor resistance
posts.authors: Mathey-Andrews N, Rodriguez CL, Shui B, et al.
posts.summary: Using mouse models of Kras-driven lung adenocarcinoma treated with KRAS inhibitors, the authors model both KRAS-dependent and KRAS-independent resistance. Genetic Kras amplification arises with continued treatment, while squamous lineage transformation gives oncogene-independent resistance.
key_points: Residual tumour after initial treatment transcriptionally resembles alveolar epithelial cells.
ΔNp63 is sufficient to push alveolar organoids to a squamous state that ignores KRAS inhibition; Nkx2-1 loss and ectopic Sox2 poise tumours for squamous commitment in vivo.
Squamous-transformed tumours show no KRAS/MAPK reactivation, pointing to lineage transcription factors as the cause of KRAS independence.

posts.title: Single-allele nanoscale mapping of regulatory variants
posts.authors: Hamley JC, Zhang W, Willmott D, et al.
posts.summary: The authors developed MCCv, a Micro Capture-C platform that reads single-allele chromatin structure to link regulatory variants to their target genes. They applied it to 405 cis-regulatory elements tied to immune-mediated inflammatory disease in CD4 T cells.
key_points: MCCv can phase heterozygous variants to connect regulatory variants with allelically imbalanced expression, and reads variant effects on chromatin contacts after genome editing.
It found a gain-of-function mechanism where a neo-CTCF motif blocks super-enhancer contacts with the SESN3 promoter and raises autoimmunity risk.
SESN3 regulates mTOR by sensing tryptophan, and mouse models support its role in autoimmunity.

posts.title: Machine learning and statistical methods for molecular quantitative trait loci
posts.authors: Engelhardt BE, Weinstock JS, Nyquist SK, et al.
posts.summary: This review covers statistical and machine-learning methods for mapping molecular quantitative trait loci (molQTLs), such as genetic effects on gene expression or chromatin accessibility. It focuses on how these methods improve standard mapping, downstream analyses and mechanistic insight.
key_points: Larger cohorts and more molecular phenotypes have increased the power of molQTL mapping.
Statistical models and, increasingly, machine learning are being developed for mapping and downstream analysis.
The emphasis is on understanding mechanisms linking genetic variation to phenotype in a gene regulatory context.

posts.title: GLM-Prior: a genomic language model for transferable sequence-derived priors in gene regulatory network inference
posts.authors: Skok Gibbs C, Chen A, Bonneau R, et al.
posts.summary: GLM-Prior is a genomic language model fine-tuned to predict transcription factor-target gene interactions from nucleotide sequence. It supplies sequence-derived priors for gene regulatory network inference when curated priors are missing.
key_points: Paired with PMF-GRN, it combines sequence-derived priors with single-cell expression for prior-conditioned network inference.
Across six cell-line contexts, it beats accessibility-based priors in four of five mammalian cell lines.
Prior quality largely limits network inference performance, and species-transfer training gives informative priors across related mammals.

posts.title: Mapping genetic regulation of gene expression to cellular contexts identifies long non-coding RNAs associated with brain disorders
posts.authors: Jia Y, Chen L, Song L, et al.
posts.summary: The authors map interaction eQTLs for long non-coding RNAs in cortical RNA-seq from 2,443 individuals, using deconvolution-derived cell-type proportions. This gives cell-context-dependent genetic regulation without single-nucleus data.
key_points: 3,763 of 17,541 analysed lncRNAs have cellular-context-dependent effects, and 74% of those are not annotated by GENCODE.
Colocalisation with GWAS of brain-related traits gives 118 lncRNA-trait events, about two-thirds detectable only after modelling cell context.
The result is a map for nominating lncRNAs that may mediate genetic risk for brain disorders.

posts.title: pileup-hi: an ultra-high-throughput, customizable alignment pileup program for large datasets
posts.authors: Piliper E, Greninger AL
posts.summary: pileup-hi is a multi-threaded alignment pileup engine built for billions of reads and high-depth clinical sequencing, where variants down to 0.01% may be called. It also supports custom output formats.
key_points: In mpileup format it is up to 13x faster than samtools mpileup, 3.2x faster than sambamba mpileup and up to 8x faster than perbase base-depth.
Aimed at time-sensitive uses such as cancer screening on Illumina NovaSeq X and Ultima UG 100 data.

posts.title: scLDM: a conditional diffusion framework for single-cell perturbation prediction
posts.authors: Wu B, Liu Y, Cheng Y, et al.
posts.summary: scLDM predicts single-cell responses to perturbations with a latent diffusion model. A variational autoencoder compresses expression, and a conditional diffusion process generates post-perturbation states guided by cell state, cell type and perturbation.
key_points: Tested on six datasets spanning drugs, viral and helminth infection, genetic perturbations and multi-species immune responses, with better accuracy than state-of-the-art methods.
Learned perturbation embeddings align with known biological mechanisms.

posts.title: Urine cell-free RNA for bladder cancer detection and treatment response prediction
posts.authors: Liu KJ, Shi WY, Nesselbush MC, et al.
posts.summary: The authors describe uRARE-seq, a liquid-biopsy method that profiles urine cell-free RNA, and apply it to 683 urine samples from patients with cancer and controls. It detects tumour-derived transcripts in prostate, kidney and bladder cancer.
key_points: It detects localised bladder cancer with 95% sensitivity at 90% specificity, outperforming urine tumour DNA analysis and unaffected by field-effect mutations.
It detects minimal residual disease and separates complete molecular responses after surgery from those after BCG.
Pretreatment urine from BCG responders is enriched for T cell signatures, and a biomarker built in 114 patients predicts likelihood of response.

posts.title: Meso-scale spatial analysis of papilloma formation and clonal expansion in cancerized skin
posts.authors: Busa VF, Behm M, Baeza-Centurion P, et al.
posts.summary: Using the two-stage DMBA/TPA mouse skin model, the authors profile genotype and transcriptome from the same coordinate-registered 1-mm punches across several centimetres, plus matched single-cell RNA-seq. This links clonal selection to local transcriptional programs.
key_points: All sequenced papillomas carried a driver mutation, but the driver was necessary and not sufficient for tumorigenesis within the study period.
Field-level signalling is rewired before tumours appear: TNF-associated necroptosis rises broadly and TGFB activity becomes spatially 'rugged', measured by a new Laplacian-based score.
Papillomas sit at local TGFB signalling minima.

posts.title: Diagnostic yield of cancer predisposition in a nationwide prospective childhood acute leukemia cohort
posts.authors: Taylan F, Staffas A, Sjögren S, et al.
posts.summary: In a nationwide prospective study of 181 children with acute leukaemia, the authors tested germline whole-genome sequencing with a 189-gene panel, plus tumour sequencing of positive cases and trio-WGS in 11 high-suspicion families.
key_points: Nine patients (about 5%) had pathogenic germline alterations: six leukaemia predisposition syndromes (TP53, CEBPA, DNMT3A, trisomy 21) and three solid tumour syndromes (MSH6, PALB2, SDHA).
Six of the nine diagnoses were previously unrecognised; findings changed surveillance in 8 of 9 patients and treatment in 4 of 9.
The diagnostic yield is modest but actionable.

posts.title: Persistent chromatin alterations and gene expression reprogramming follow widespread DNA damage in glioblastoma
posts.authors: Modrek AS, Chandradoss KR, Do C, et al.
posts.summary: The authors introduced many simultaneous Cas9-induced double-strand breaks at defined sites in glioblastoma cells and followed genetic and non-genetic changes over time. This models widespread DNA damage such as chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
key_points: Megabase-scale changes persisted two weeks after damage, including a shift from transient intra-TAD contacts to lasting long-range cis and trans contacts.
Gene expression changed and large structural variants appeared.
The findings suggest widespread DNA damage can leave long-term genetic and non-genetic changes that may affect tumour outcome and resistance.

posts.title: Isolated clival Langerhans cell histiocytosis in a pediatric patient: systematic review and illustrative case report
posts.authors: Abdallah AM, Hulliel AF, Dabash TY, et al.
posts.summary: The authors report a 3.5-year-old boy with isolated clival Langerhans cell histiocytosis and add a PRISMA systematic review of 11 published cases. Chordoma appears here as a skull base tumour that the lesion can mimic on imaging.
key_points: Osteolytic clival lesions mimicked chordoma and other skull base tumours; abducens palsy and diplopia were the most common symptoms.
Histology showed typical LCH with CD1a and S100 positivity, so biopsy confirmation is essential.
Management varied (biopsy, resection, chemotherapy, radiotherapy) and outcomes were mostly favourable.

posts.title: Nailpolish: Reference-free UMI deduplication and consensus read generation
posts.authors: Cheng OY, Tan JW, Davidson NM
posts.summary: Nailpolish is a fast, reference-free tool that error-corrects and deduplicates UMI-tagged long reads by building consensus sequences with partial order alignment. It also separates false duplicates caused by UMI collisions.
key_points: Tested on eleven Oxford Nanopore and PacBio datasets spanning bulk, single-cell, spatial and targeted protocols.
It lowered per-read error rates and outperformed existing deduplication tools.

posts.title: Accurate isoform quantification in bulk and single-cell RNA-seq by integrating multi-platform sequencing data and sequence-to-expression models
posts.authors: Apostolides M, Wang J, Saberi A, et al.
posts.summary: MPAQT is a probabilistic framework that combines short- and long-read RNA-seq while modelling each platform's biases. It quantifies transcript isoforms in bulk and single-cell data.
key_points: It gives state-of-the-art isoform quantification from short reads alone, and improves further when short and long reads are analysed jointly.
Sequence-to-expression models (RNA-binding protein motifs, co-expression) can be added as priors, improving single-cell quantification.
The models point to isoform-specific UTR sequence features as strong contributors to isoform abundance and exon usage.

posts.title: DECIPHER integrates disentangled representation learning and prototype-based cell-type deconvolution across molecular modalities
posts.authors: Lai W, Li C, Deng Q, et al.
posts.summary: DECIPHER is an end-to-end deep-learning framework for cell-type deconvolution of bulk omics that works across molecular modalities. It learns a domain-constant representation for deconvolution and a domain-specific one for batch-like variation.
key_points: Nonlinear representation learning is combined with differentiable non-negative least squares to estimate cell-type proportions.
It performs robustly on simulations, experimental bulk mixtures and real datasets.
The learned representation also supports age prediction across cohorts and prognostic stratification in lung adenocarcinoma.

posts.title: Benchmarking niche identification via domain segmentation for spatial transcriptomics data
posts.authors: Wang Y, Chen Y, Yang L, et al.
posts.summary: The authors annotated single-cell-resolution CosMx data of a human follicular lymphoid hyperplasia lymph node as a reference. They benchmarked 16 domain segmentation algorithms for finding tissue niches.
key_points: Most methods in default settings fail to recover biologically defined niche boundaries.
Stochastic infiltration of peripheral cell types lowers the spatial signal-to-noise ratio, which prioritises local variance over architecture.
Weighting core functional lineages restores niche resolution in some frameworks.

posts.title: A gene program association study (GPAS) delineates novel patterns of lineage plasticity and aggressiveness in non-small cell lung cancer
posts.authors: Campbell JD, Hong R, Klockner P, et al.
posts.summary: The authors built an atlas of gene co-expression modules in cancer cells from 127 primary NSCLCs using a new framework, GPAS, and linked the modules to clinical and histopathological features.
key_points: Lung adenocarcinoma shows extensive lineage infidelity, with modules from several alveolar cell types; late-stage modules appear in early-stage tumours.
Basal- and squamous-like cells are proposed intermediates in invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma.
A new squamous subtype has lower canonical squamous modules and higher fibrinogen; squamous modules also appear in smoke-exposed normal basal cells.

posts.title: Three-Year Longitudinal Analysis of Splicing Changes in Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1
posts.authors: Legare C, Planco L, Merritt R, et al.
posts.summary: The authors measured a splicing index (SI) by targeted RNA-seq in vastus lateralis biopsies from 20 people with myotonic dystrophy type 1, taken three years apart, to see how splicing dysregulation progresses.
key_points: Baseline SI correlated with percent predicted muscle strength in ankle, knee and hand-grip muscles.
SI worsened on average, but progression varied widely between participants; adult versus juvenile phenotype and lower baseline SI were linked to faster progression.
The authors say clinical phenotype and baseline severity should be considered when reading longitudinal SI in trials.

posts.title: RNA-sequencing as an expression-informed alternative for somatic variant detection and cancer driver identification
posts.authors: Akutagawa J, Mak AJ, Damle T, et al.
posts.summary: The authors called somatic variants and cancer drivers from tumour RNA-seq alone in 1,359 PCAWG and TCGA samples that have matched WGS.
key_points: RNA-seq alone found at least one putative driver gene in 15 of 16 cancer types, consistent with WGS-based predictions.
Variant allele frequency of RNA-derived variants reflects predicted functional impact.
The work offers a pan-cancer resource of RNA-seq-derived variants.

posts.title: Accurate and scalable demultiplexing of single-cell RNA sequencing using BEACON
posts.authors: Ji BW, Lammers M, Houser A, et al.
posts.summary: BEACON is a sample demultiplexing method for barcode-multiplexed single-cell RNA-seq. It learns the background count distribution from the data and removes it from each cell, improving classification.
key_points: It outperforms other state-of-the-art methods on several human datasets.
Applied to cancer cell line time courses, it helped identify genes associated with aggressive tumours in vivo.
Adapted to protein-transcriptome profiling, it improves protein signal recovery and found a CD161-positive effector memory CD4 T cell population that was validated.

posts.title: Hyper-mutational processes provide a head-start for weak cancer drivers: explaining atypical KRAS variants
posts.authors: Nicholson MD, Tomlinson I
posts.summary: Using mathematical modelling, the authors show that aberrant mutational processes alone can explain why hypermutant cancers carry weak rather than canonical driver mutations.
key_points: Raising the mutation rate per cell division, without changing selection, can let weak drivers dominate because further driver events arrive quickly.
